title: Rochester Chamber Launches 5-Year Economic Growth Initiative - Quick Country 96.5
content: Rochester, MN (KROC-AM News) - The Rochester Area Chamber of Commerce today announced the launch of a five-year economic development initiative. A news release issued by the business organization describes Momentum30 as a coordinated effort to "ensure the region can drive the momentum to attract talent, support business growth, advocate for economic prosperity, and capitalize on emerging opportunities." “Momentum30 establishes a strategic plan to support the growth of the Rochester area, ensuring we maximize our region’s long-term potential,” said Gwen Stevens, chair of the Rochester Area Chamber of Commerce Board, Momentum30 Advisory Committee member, and president and CEO of People’s Energy Cooperative. “Investment in Momentum30 will enhance the Rochester Area Chamber of Commerce’s impact on priorities essential to our community’s economic vitality and resiliency – Talent Attraction & Retention, Business Recruitment & Retention, and Advocacy.” According to the Chamber, a key component of the initiative will be the launch of a regional talent attraction campaign. The news release says it will "position Rochester to compete for highly skilled workers in an increasingly competitive labor market." The campaign will promote the community's "quality of life, career opportunities, and unique strengths." The business group's statement says Momentum30 will also focus on attracting new businesses and supporting existing employers. “Momentum30 will enhance our community’s ability to attract industry and new business opportunities to the Rochester area through the addition of vital, proactive business strategies that complement the development resources and partners of our region during this exciting time of growth,” said Tom Leimer, Rochester Area Chamber of Commerce Board member, Momentum30 Advisory Committee chair, and senior vice president/general manager, Knutson Construction. The Chamber of Commerce statement also notes that it has already secured 80% of the more than $1.3 million investment needed for the Momentum30 initiative.

title: Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), TSMC (NYSE: TSM), and AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) Approach Buy Zones In Tuesday Trading - foreignpolicyjournal.com
content: By Ewan Scott | Sep 15, 2026 | Economy & Business, Featured, News & Analysis Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), the Dow Jones technology heavyweight, moved into or near a buy zone during Tuesday’s market session alongside several other major names. Nvidia chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (NYSE: TSM) also featured prominently among stocks trading at technically significant price levels during the session. Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) posted a gain of 2.19% on the day, making it one of the stronger performers among the group of stocks approaching buy territory. Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE) rounded out the group, advancing 0.89% as investor interest in clean energy infrastructure stocks continued to build alongside semiconductor and technology names. Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) slipped 0.52% during the session, though the stock remained positioned within a notable technical range that traders closely monitor for entry opportunities. Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) gained 0.57%, reflecting continued market confidence in the artificial intelligence chip ecosystem that has driven semiconductor valuations higher over recent periods. TSMC (NYSE: TSM) declined 1.02% on the day, though the stock remained near levels that investors and analysts have identified as a potential buying opportunity given its central role in global chip supply. The clustering of major technology and energy names near buy zones on the same trading day reflects broader market momentum that has supported growth and innovation-oriented equities in recent months. Buy zones, as used in technical analysis, typically refer to price ranges just above a key breakout point from a recognized chart pattern, offering traders a defined entry with manageable downside risk. The presence of both semiconductor-linked stocks and a clean energy name like Bloom Energy in the same conversation underscores the widening scope of investor appetite beyond pure-play artificial intelligence plays. Analysts continue to watch whether stocks like AMD and TSMC can sustain momentum above key technical levels as global demand for advanced chips remains robust across data center, automotive, and consumer markets. Market participants will be monitoring Tuesday’s price action closely as an indicator of whether the current rally in technology stocks has sufficient breadth to extend further into the trading week. title: Billings Auction Features Vintage Chuck E. Cheese Arcade Games - billingsmix.com
content: The late Oscar Cooke started moving a modest collection of old tractors and farm equipment to a rural property on the outskirts of Billings in 1964. Like many collectors, a few pieces here and there eventually became a lot of stuff. Soon, Cooke and his wife Marcella had assembled an authentic replica of an early Montana town. Named "Cookeville," the town at Oscar's Dreamland once had a narrow-gauge train that circled the property and an operational 1920 Ferris wheel. Oscar's Dreamland was a tourist attraction in the summer months, drawing fans with its concessions, a museum, a Model T garage, a general store, and a variety of other historic buildings and displays. Read More: Here's How You Could Win $25,000 This Fall After Oscar Cooke passed away in 1995, the IRS came calling in 1998, forcing a liquidation of much of the equipment and antiques and a name change from Oscar's Dreamland to Oscar's Park. Collectors from 44 states and 17 countries attended that auction. Today, the property retains much of the former Cookeville town, and there are still hundreds (perhaps thousands?) of pieces of history dotting the footprint. Oscar Cooke's daughter, Marcie Cooke Limpp, and her husband still own and operate Oscar's Park, which nowadays is mostly utilized as a wedding venue and for other special events. A collector in her own right, affable Marcie told me how they came to possess a collection of what appear to be early 90s Chuck E. Cheese games from the Billings location. It was a prime example of right-time, right-place. An electrician friend of Limpp's was working on the lights at Chuck E. Cheese around 15 years ago. He called her up and said, "You gotta get over here right now, and bring a truck and trailer. They're getting ready to dispose of a bunch of games." So she did. Marcie said the time has come for them to downsize a bit from their massive collection, and they'll be parting with the Chuck E. Cheese games, along with hundreds of other collectibles and antiques on October 10th. The live, in-person (and by phone) Limpp Family Auction will be hosted by Rick Young & Sons. The auction kicks off at 10 AM on October 10th at Oscar's Park, 3740 Wise Lane. While the retro Chuck E. Cheese games are what caught my eye (I mean... who wouldn't want a full-sized Skeeball machine in their basement!?), fans of antique Montana agricultural equipment and other collectibles will certainly be in attendance too.

title: Taiwan Semiconductor Issues Blunt Warning on AI - TradingView
content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing TSM is striking a more cautious tone on artificial intelligence even as the chipmaker remains one of the biggest financial beneficiaries of the AI boom. A senior executive warned that the technology is powerful but still immature, underscoring a growing tension for investors: TSMC is supplying the chips driving AI adoption while remaining reluctant to deploy the technology deeply inside its own most sensitive operations. AI is like a three-year old superman. It can be quite powerful, but it doesn't know what kind of damage it can inflict, TSMC co-chief operating officer Y.J. Mii told students at National Taiwan University. And it doesn't know right from wrong, he added. Mii said TSMC remains wary of using AI with confidential research and development data because improper deployment could lead to information leaks or data loss. His comments come as the broader technology industry debates whether frontier AI development should slow while safety controls catch up. Recent incidents involving rogue AI agents accessing external systems have intensified those concerns. Mii also said current AI systems provide limited assistance in developing cutting-edge chipmaking processes, where progress depends heavily on physics, manufacturing constraints and access to increasingly advanced equipment. That distinction matters because TSMC sits at the center of the AI supply chain. Nvidia NVDA, Apple AAPL and other major customers depend on its leading-edge manufacturing capacity, making protection of proprietary process technology critical to maintaining the company's competitive moat. Mii's comments do not weaken the near-term AI demand story for TSMC, but they highlight how differently AI may affect chipmakers internally versus externally. Investors should watch whether Nvidia and other customers continue accelerating advanced-node demand, as well as TSMC's capacity expansion, pricing and margins. The bigger risk would be a slowdown in AI infrastructure spending, not TSMC's cautious internal adoption. Continued strong demand for advanced chips would keep the investment case intact, while weaker hyperscaler spending or slower model development could eventually pressure utilization and growth expectations. title: Meta Looks to Slash Its AI Bill With Homegrown Silicon - TradingView
content: Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ) plans to deploy its latest in-house artificial intelligence chip in data centers during the first half of 2027. The company expects the processors to cut costs and energy use as its AI infrastructure expands, Bloomberg reported Monday. Meta is testing the third generation of its chip line, MTIA 450, code-named Arke. The company first announced its custom AI chip plans in 2023. Its next processor, MTIA 500, code-named Astrid, should complete design work in about a month. Meta expects to deploy it by the end of 2027. Meta is working with Broadcom Inc. www.benzinga.com/quote/AVGO(NASDAQ:AVGO) on chip designs and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Ltd. www.benzinga.com/quote/TSM(NYSE:TSM) on production. The effort could reduce Meta’s reliance on NVIDIA Corporation https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVDA(NASDAQ:NVDA) processors. Yee Jiun Song, Meta’s vice president of engineering, said the custom chips aim to deliver better performance per watt and per dollar. Separately, Meta on Tuesday launched Meta One, a subscription service offering expanded AI access and premium features across Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp and Meta AI. The core experience will remain free. Meta One launches with more than 50 features and has recorded 15 million subscriptions and trials to date. Paid plans offer higher AI usage, including image and video generation, as well as tools for creators and businesses. Plans are available globally. Single-product subscriptions start at $2.99 per month, individual bundles at $7.99 and creator and business bundles at $14.99. Meta stock was little changed on Tuesday as megacap growth stocks faced a broader risk-off session. The Nasdaq fell 0.60%, while the S&P 500 lost 0.52%. Meta’s relative strength index stands at 71.02, putting the stock in overbought territory. An RSI above 70 can signal increased pullback risk after a strong rally. The longer-term setup remains mixed. The stock still carries a death cross from December 2025, when its 50-day SMA moved below the 200-day SMA. Therefore, it could remain volatile until its longer-term averages strengthen. Key resistance sits near $673, while support is around $556.50. Meta carries a Buy consensus rating with an average price forecast of $774.58. Wedbush maintained a Neutral rating on Sept. 14 and raised its price forecast to $650. JPMorgan upgraded Meta to Overweight on Sept. 10 and raised its price forecast to $820. On Sept. 1, Wedbush maintained Neutral with a $595 price forecast. The stock trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of 25.1. Meta’s Benzinga Edge scorecard shows strong Growth and Quality scores of 79.54 and 71.43, respectively. Momentum stands at 42.53, while Value is 49.76. The readings point to a growth-and-quality profile. However, moderate momentum and an overbought RSI suggest the stock could consolidate after its recent rally. The First Trust Dow Jones Internet Index Fund https://www.benzinga.com/quote/FDN(NYSE:FDN) has a 9.46% Meta weighting. The Invesco AI and Next Gen Software ETF https://www.benzinga.com/quote/IGPT(NYSE:IGPT) holds 8.91%, while the Global X Social Media ETF https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SOCL(NASDAQ:SOCL) has an 8.76% weighting. title: TSMC Slips as 2-Nanometer Chip Powers a 51% AI Leap - TradingView
content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing TSM, the world's largest contract chipmaker, slipped roughly 0.4% to $416.60 Tuesday as MediaTek rolled out the first Dimensity processor built on TSMC's cutting-edge 2-nanometer process. The Dimensity 9600 Pro is aimed squarely at premium smartphones from Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo, giving TSMC's newest manufacturing node an early showcase in one of the world's biggest consumer-chip markets. MediaTek's announcement says the new processor delivers 51% higher large-language-model prefill performance, 55% more token generation per watt and 61% lower multicore power consumption versus its predecessor. Smartphones powered by the chip are expected to arrive this quarter. Those are MediaTek's own test results, so real-world devices will ultimately determine how much of that performance survives outside the lab. Still, the launch puts TSMC's 2-nanometer technology directly into the AI-on-device race rather than leaving it as a manufacturing roadmap story. The valuation picture adds a note of caution. At $416.60, TSMC trades 14.65% above its GuruFocus GF Value of $363.38, suggesting investors are already paying a meaningful premium for future growth. TSMC generated $40.2 billion of second-quarter revenue with a 67.7% gross margin, while 2-nanometer products represented only 3% of wafer revenue. MediaTek gives the technology an important commercial proof point, but the bigger question is scale: yields, wafer pricing and customer volume will determine whether 2-nanometer moves from an impressive technical milestone into TSMC's next major earnings engine. title: TSMC's Strong August Revenues Signal Continued AI-Driven Chip Demand - TradingView
content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company TSM, or TSMC, announced its consolidated net revenues for August 2026 of approximately New Taiwan Dollar (NT$) 514.81 billion, marking a 10.1% increase from July 2026 and a 53.3% rise from August 2025. Cumulative revenues from January through August 2026 reached NT$3,386.87 billion, representing 39.3% growth compared to the same period in 2025. The latest monthly performance reflects that the company continues to benefit from strong demand for its leading-edge process technologies. High-performance computing (HPC) continues to account for the biggest share of TSMC’s business, benefiting from rising data needs and the expansion of AI applications. The platform accounted for 66% of second-quarter 2026 revenues and grew 20% sequentially. The company also saw growth across Internet of Things (IoT), Digital Consumer Electronics (“DCE”) and Automotive, with revenues increasing 4%, 5% and 15%, respectively, from the prior quarter. TSMC’s technology mix remains heavily weighted toward advanced process technologies, with 7-nanometer and below accounting for 77% of wafer revenues in the second quarter. The 2-nanometer process contributed 3%, while 3-nanometer, 5-nanometer and 7-nanometer accounted for 30%, 33% and 11%, respectively. Management continues to point to robust AI-related demand, as the AI megatrend continues to drive the need for more computing and leading-edge silicon. Strong demand signals from customers, particularly cloud service providers, continue to support TSMC’s view of a multiyear AI opportunity. The company also sees another source of silicon demand emerging from Agentic AI, which is increasing the role of CPUs in AI data centers alongside AI accelerators. TSMC is working closely with CPU customers across x86, ARM-based and RISC-V architectures to support these opportunities with advanced technologies and capacity. GlobalFoundries GFS has entered into a long-term manufacturing agreement with Monolithic Power Systems, under which MPS’ proprietary process technology will be deployed at GFS’ advanced 300mm manufacturing facility in Singapore. The collaboration is expected to help GlobalFoundries expand manufacturing capacity for critical power management solutions serving high-growth markets beginning in early 2027. The company finalized a definitive agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce’s CHIPS Research and Development Office for a $375 million R&D award to accelerate its Quantum Technology Solutions business. Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. QCOM has entered into a multi-generation collaboration with Amazon to enable customized silicon at scale for large-scale AI data centers, working together on AI inference. The companies are also developing optical connectivity solutions of up to 1.6T and future-generation solutions. Qualcomm recently expanded its Dragonwing portfolio with highly integrated platforms designed to broaden access to intelligent edge computing across consumer, commercial and industrial segments. Over the past 12 months, TSMC shares have rallied 60% compared with the industry’s 65.8% growth. TSM currently trades at a forward 12-month Price/Sales (P/S) of 10.63X compared with its historical median of 11.08X and the industry average of 11.02X. Estimates for TSMC’s earnings have seen steady upward revisions over the past three months. TSMC sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) at present. content: The wide moat strategy involves investing in companies that not only lead their industries but are also strategically fortified to maintain dominance in the future. These companies possess durable competitive advantages that shield them from competitors. This investment strategy focuses on companies with unique strengths such as brand recognition, patent protection, proprietary technology and network effects. These moats ensure long-term profitability and market leadership, making the companies resilient in volatile markets. Here we recommend five non-tech Wide Moat stocks with a favorable Zacks Rank. These stocks are: Caterpillar Inc. CAT, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd. TSM, UnitedHealth Group Inc. UNH, Teradyne Inc. TER and Zebra Technologies Corp. ZBRA. Each of our picks currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). You can see the complete list of today’s Zacks #1 Rank stocks here. Caterpillar has been benefiting from broad demand across construction, mining and power markets, with rising sales to users and a record backlog. CAT’s order backlog reached a record $72 billion at the end of second-quarter 2026, up 92% year over year. Caterpillar is gaining from rising artificial intelligence (AI) data-center-related power demand. As big technology companies establish data centers globally to support their generative AI applications, CAT is witnessing robust order levels for reciprocating engines for data centers. CAT expects full-year 2026 power generation growth in both reciprocating engines and Solar Turbines as cloud computing and generative AI support data-center build-outs. The company continues to add capacity against this multi-year opportunity. CAT’s long-term plan calls for large reciprocating engine capacity nearly three times the 2024 levels and Power Generation sales more than three times the 2024 levels by 2030. It is also restarting a 10-megawatt gas reciprocating engine platform, adding about 1.5 gigawatts of capacity with shipments expected from fourth-quarter 2026. ZBRA’s expanding transportation and logistics pipeline also supports future growth opportunities. Grace Costa finished with three singles and two RBIs for Destin Commons. Michael Costa hit four singles for three RBIs, and Rob Carrizales hit two doubles and a single for two RBIs. Cozmo Starnes belted a home run. Corey Armstrong led Beau Esprit with two homers, a double and a single for six RBIs. Neil Barlow hit three singles for an RBI, and Noah Bailey ripped an inside-the-park homer and two singles for an RBI. Roman Donofro connected for a home run.

title: Amazon and 2 Other AI Stocks to Buy With $5,000 - The Motley Fool
content: Three layers of the AI build-out, one basket -- and the most money goes to the steadiest layer, not the fastest-growing one. The artificial intelligence (AI) build-out isn't a single trade. The money flows through layers: Cloud platforms rent out computing capacity, a foundry manufactures the chips underneath it, and data center builders put up the buildings that house all of it. That means an investor with $5,000 to put to work doesn't have to bet on one layer. I'd split the money across three stocks -- Amazon (AMZN -2.02%), Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM -1.02%), and a small slice of Applied Digital (APLD -4.72%). Each contributes something the other two can't. Amazon gets the biggest slice because it pairs a fast-growing AI business with the profits to pay for it. Our team of credit card pros don’t just recommend this card—they actually use it. Motley Fool Money calls it a top pick for a reason. Amazon's cloud computing segment, Amazon Web Services (AWS), hasn't grown this fast in 18 quarters. Second-quarter revenue rose 37% year over year, reaching $42.2 billion, and the segment turned that growth into $16.6 billion of operating income, up about 64%. In other words, the cloud layer of the build-out is accelerating -- and profitably. Even so, AWS is only about a fifth of Amazon's revenue. The rest comes mostly from retail and advertising, which gives the stock a footing the pure AI plays lack. When our analyst team has a stock tip, it can pay to listen. After all, Stock Advisor’s total average return is 949%* — a market-crushing outperformance compared to 212% for the S&P 500. They just revealed what they believe are the 10 best stocks for investors to buy right now, available when you join Stock Advisor. The spending is heavy, to be sure. Free cash flow ran about $7.6 billion negative over the trailing 12 months, mostly because of the company's AI infrastructure investments. But that kind of spending is exactly what the other two stocks in this basket get paid from. Shares trade at about 24 times forecast earnings for next year, the basket's most ordinary valuation on its most diversified business. That seems a reasonable price for an anchor. Whoever wins the AI chip race, chip foundry giant Taiwan Semiconductor manufactures advanced processors for most of the leading designers. Owning the foundry means not having to guess which chip design comes out on top. Demand has been climbing. Revenue was up 36% year over year in the second quarter, then 45% in July, and then 53% in August, a monthly record of NT$514.8 billion (about $16 billion). Notably, revenue through the first eight months of 2026 is running 39% ahead of the same period last year. The work is lucrative, too, with a gross margin of 67.7% in the second quarter. At about $431 as of this writing, shares trade at about 20 times expected earnings for next year -- a lower price-to-earnings multiple than Amazon's, for a faster-growing business. However, the discount arguably reflects concentration. TSMC's growth is tied closely to AI infrastructure spending, and its most advanced factories sit in Taiwan. If the big spenders pull back, the foundry would feel it quickly. The last slice is the smallest because the business is the least proven. Applied Digital builds AI data centers and rents them to large tenants. Tenants have signed 15-year leases on about 1.4 gigawatts of the company's capacity, contracts that total about $36 billion in future rent. Yet only 175 megawatts of that leased capacity was live when the company reported in late July. The gap between those two numbers is both the investment case and the risk. Fiscal 2026 revenue (the year ended May 31) was $611.3 million, up 167% from the year before, alongside a net loss of $249.2 million. Rent begins only as buildings are finished and handed to tenants, so nearly all of the contracted money is still ahead. And construction timelines can slip. Why include it at all? The leases are take-or-pay agreements (rent is owed even if a tenant ends up not using the capacity). And the company's stock market value is about $7.8 billion, a small fraction of what the finished portfolio is under contract to collect. If the campuses keep getting delivered on schedule, the stock could be worth far more. That uncertainty is why the position stays small. I'd put $2,500 in Amazon, $1,750 in Taiwan Semiconductor, and the final $750 in Applied Digital. Half the money goes to the steadiest layer, the company that can fund its AI ambitions from its own profitable businesses. Taiwan Semiconductor gets the next slice, offering faster growth and a cheaper price-to-earnings multiple in exchange for more concentration risk. Applied Digital gets a sliver, sized small enough that a construction delay wouldn't derail the whole plan. Of course, all three ride the same underlying trend, and a slowdown in AI infrastructure spending would hit the whole basket -- Amazon least, Applied Digital most. The lopsided split is deliberate. Ultimately, I'd rather own three layers of the build-out than one company's slice of it. I'd buy all three at these prices, in these proportions. TSMC holds a unique position in the chipmaking world, and that dominance has allowed the company to reach new heights. However, I think it's far from done setting all-time highs, and it could reach levels never before seen by the time 2027 rolls around. I think it could get all the way up to $600 per share fairly easily by the end of next year, making it a no-brainer stock to buy right now. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This is a great place to be, as it allows the company to stay neutral in the AI race and fabricate chips for competing companies (such as Nvidia and AMD). However, TSMC also has a unique position in terms of size. During 2025, research by The Motley Fool found that TSMC accounted for over 70% of chip foundry revenue in the world. That means that if one of the major AI firms wanted to switch to a different chip foundry, it probably wouldn't have enough production capacity to meet demand. The sheer size of TSMC versus its competition gives it a major competitive advantage, and it allows investors to easily project how TSMC will grow over the next few years, as it's likely to grow in lockstep with AI spending increases. Next year, Wall Street analysts expect the company's revenue to rise 34% year over year. That suggests another fantastic year for the company, and with TSMC trading at a reasonable valuation, I think it could be in for major stock price growth. TSMC tends to trade at around 28 times forward earnings as the year ends. Currently, the company trades at about 20 times next year's earnings. If TSMC can rise to 28 times forward earnings by the end of 2027, there's about 41% upside in TSMC's stock. At today's $435 price tag, that indicates a $612 stock price by the end of next year. That's great upside in one year, and given Wall Street analysts' history of underestimating TSMC's growth during the AI build-out, its true potential could be far higher.
